title: Episode 26: My Ten Least Favorite Things about Dungeon Crawl and Adventure Games
body:
https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=7NZvpCqH7eA

The mirror of Episode 2, and Daniel (@dungeondive) sets the terms carefully: this is not a list of bad games. Nearly every complaint is illustrated with something he loves, because these are the faults his favourite genre keeps committing.

Counting down: table hogs that needn't be (*Bardsung*, whose board doesn't fit his dining table); games too long for what they offer — the single most common criticism he levelled at his own top 50, and the thing most house rules exist to fix; throttled fun, where the game drip-feeds content you already paid for; too many tiles to dig through (*Mansions of Madness* 2E, which he'd play more often with fewer); components that make play harder, like *Dungeon Degenerates*' beautiful and unreadable board; a focus purely on combat, with no verb but "fight"; over-long padded campaigns; poorly written campaigns, split into weak prose and outright narrative disconnect; hundreds of unnecessary miniatures; and at number one, chits — boxes boasting "over 300 tokens," including *Shadows of Brimstone*'s, which are never used.

He then reads patron complaints: expansion bloat, setup and teardown, fiddliness, messy rulebooks, and too little that is tactically interesting. His one plea to designers: print the rule on the token.

----

Which of these ten would you forgive completely in a game you already love?
